newsitem.title: USA: Exxon begins Sakhalin I appraisal drilling.
newsitem.headline: Exxon begins Sakhalin I appraisal drilling.

text.p: Exxon Corp said Tuesday the Sakhalin I Consortium is drilling an appraisal well in the high-potential Arkutun-Dagi field offshore Sakhalin Island using Russian equipment and personnel.
The well is part of a $200-$300 million program required to better define estimates of reserves and to acquire information needed to prepare development plans for the Sakhalin I Project, Exxon said.
The well is located about 12 miles offshore in the Sea of Okhotsk, about 85 miles southeast of the city of Okha in water about 100 feet deep.
Exxon said the well will be drilled to about 8,200 feet using the Rosneft-Sakhalinmorneftegas "OKHA" jack-up rig.

The Sakhalin I Consortium includes two Russian companies, Rosneft-Sakhalin and Sakhalinmorneftegas-Shelf, the Japanese company Sakhalin Oil and Gas Development Co Ltd, and Exxon Neftegas Limited, as operator of the project. Exxon Neftegas and SODECO each have a 30 percent interest, while Sakhalinmorneftegas-Shelf and Rosneft-Sakhalin have a 23 and 17 percent interest, respectively, Exxon said.
